title: Encoded PowerShell execution with defense evasion on WORKSTATION6
summary: User pgustavo (normally on WORKSTATION5) launched a hidden PowerShell command via wmiprvse.exe that decoded to a script disabling Script Block Logging and AMSI, then contacting external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious, outside company network) to download and execute code. This indicates active attack with defense evasion and potential malware installation.
evidence: Encoded PowerShell command -enc flag launched by wmiprvse.exe on WORKSTATION6 by user pgustavo
Decoded command attempts to disable Script Block Logging and bypass AMSI security controls
External IP 10.10.10.5 contacted - suspicious private address not in company network ranges
User pgustavo normally logs into WORKSTATION5, but attack occurred on WORKSTATION6 (unusual host)
Process chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell (encoded) -> conhost -> whoami.exe (classic evasion pattern)

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately to prevent lateral movement and data exfiltration
Force password reset for user pgustavo and investigate credential compromise, as wmiprvse.exe launch may indicate pass-the-hash or token theft
Block outbound connections to IP 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy level and investigate any other hosts contacting this IP
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated signatures, focusing on payload downloaded from 10.10.10.5
Review pgustavo's recent login history and file access on both WORKSTATION5 and WORKSTATION6 to determine full scope of compromise

title: Remote WMI Execution with Encoded PowerShell and Defense Evasion on WORKSTATION6
summary: Attacker used pgustavo's valid credentials to remotely execute PowerShell via WMI (wmiprvse.exe) on WORKSTATION6, launching an encoded command that disabled Script Block Logging, bypassed AMSI antivirus, and downloaded malicious code from 10.10.10.5. The user's normal host is WORKSTATION5, suggesting possible account compromise or lateral movement.
evidence: WMI remote execution (wmiprvse.exe launched powershell.exe) as pgustavo at 04:14:55
Network logon by pgustavo from 172.18.39.5 synchronous with process execution
PowerShell launched with -enc flag (obfuscated/base64 encoded command)
Decoded command disables Script Block Logging and bypasses AMSI
Command contacts URL http://10.10.10.5 for downloads
pgustavo is a Domain user (lab) with normal host WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
whoami.exe executed by PowerShell confirming command execution success
related_to_prior: ALERT-001 was an earlier encoded PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6 with defense evasion - this appears to be a continuation or escalation of the same attack chain, possibly the same attacker using the same encoding technique

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately to prevent lateral movement
Reset pgustavo's credentials and enforce MFA reset
Block IOC IP 10.10.10.5 at perimeter and investigate any outbound connections
Full forensic analysis of WORKSTATION6 including disk imaging
Review all other hosts pgustavo has accessed recently for similar WMI/PowerShell patterns
Update WMI remote execution monitoring and Script Block Logging policies

This is part of a confirmed attack chain with two prior true positive alerts (ALERT-001, ALERT-002) on the same host.
